The bracket-interior letter in U16 is an open returning curve; U17 is a low open cup/oval with separated upper ends. Neither shows the same clear tall-stem/closed-loop construction. U19 is already locally preserved as a u-shaped formal-variable mark. T065/T066 and their S035 copies currently print k[b] with no local qualification for U16/U17.

provisional_candidates.support: They occur in the preceding operator-action discussion, and the next sentence asserts a faithful action.
provisional_candidates.limit: The image alone does not show the high stem and closed loop found in the earlier b, so direct clear-b transcription would overstate the glyph evidence.

provisional_candidates.reading: Preserve the low open curve or u-shaped mark literally; explain the intended operator image separately.
provisional_candidates.support: It covers the visible two distinct low curved forms without forcing a closed loop.
provisional_candidates.limit: If u is taken as an independent polynomial variable rather than an operator name, the faithful-action statement needs correction: evaluation on finite-dimensional V has a nonzero kernel.

forward_validation: The subalgebra of actual endomorphisms generated by b acts faithfully by evaluation: an operator killing every v is zero. This establishes the intended image algebra, while the source marks remain locally described.
backward_validation: The full polynomial ring k[U] acting via U mapped to b is not faithful on finite-dimensional V: finite-dimensional End_k(V) gives a nonzero annihilating polynomial; if V=0, 1 already kills all of V. Hence a literal u-shaped mark cannot by itself justify calling the full polynomial-ring action faithful.
